name: ax_slotted_boss_flange
title: Slotted boss flange (exercise T9)
story: A shaft in the 26 mm bore pushes sideways with 3 kN, trying to bend the boss over. The flange is bolted down.

material.name: Iron, Gray (EN-GJL-250: E 110 GPa; cast iron has no yield point, so its 250 MPa tensile strength is used)

steps.title: Open the Stress Analysis environment
steps.command: Environments tab > Begin panel > Stress Analysis
actions: Open the part (slotted boss flange) in Inventor.
Click the Environments tab, then Stress Analysis. The Stress Analysis tab opens.
steps.note: The study here: A shaft in the 26 mm bore pushes sideways with 3 kN, trying to bend the boss over. The flange is bolted down.

steps.title: Create a static study
steps.command: Stress Analysis tab > Manage panel > Create Simulation
actions: Click Create Simulation. Give it a name, for example "Slotted boss flange (exercise T9) load test".
Simulation Type: Static Analysis. Design Objective: Single Point. Click OK.

steps.title: Assign the material
steps.command: Stress Analysis tab > Material panel > Assign
actions: Click Assign. In the Override Material column pick Iron, Gray (EN-GJL-250: E 110 GPa; cast iron has no yield point, so its 250 MPa tensile strength is used).
Check its properties in the Material Browser: Young's modulus 110 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.26, yield strength 250 MPa.
Click OK.
steps.note: The results below use these values. If your library values differ, your answers will differ a little.

steps.title: Fix the part
steps.command: Stress Analysis tab > Constraints panel > Fixed
actions: Click Fixed and pick the underside of the flange.
Click OK. A Fixed Constraint appears in the browser under Constraints.
steps.note: A fixed constraint stops the face moving in any direction. It stands in for the bolts, the bench or the wall.

steps.title: Apply the load: force
steps.command: Stress Analysis tab > Loads panel > Force
actions: Click Force and pick the 26 mm bore.
Set: Force, 3000 N, sideways (+X). Use the Direction button and Flip if the arrow points the wrong way.
Click OK.
steps.note: The arrows show where the load acts and which way.

steps.title: Set up and view the mesh
steps.command: Stress Analysis tab > Prepare panel > Mesh Settings, then Mesh View
actions: Click Mesh Settings. Average Element Size 0.1, Minimum Element Size 0.2, Grading Factor 1.5, Maximum Turn Angle 60 degrees. Tick Create Curved Mesh Elements. Click OK.
Click Mesh View. Inventor splits the part into small tetrahedra (four sided elements).
Look for small elements round holes and fillets: that is where stress changes fastest.
steps.note: Sizes in Mesh Settings are a fraction of the part size, not millimetres. The hub mesh: 27528 elements, 47941 nodes, about 4.62 mm across.

steps.title: Converge the answer (optional)
steps.command: Stress Analysis tab > Prepare panel > Convergence Settings
actions: Click Convergence Settings. Set Maximum Number of h Refinements to 2 and Stop Criteria to 10 %.
Inventor then refines the mesh where the stress is highest and solves again, until the answer changes by less than 10 %.
steps.note: A finer mesh gives a more trustworthy peak stress, but takes longer to solve.

steps.title: Run the simulation
steps.command: Stress Analysis tab > Solve panel > Simulate
actions: Click Simulate, then Run.
When it finishes, the results appear in the browser under Results.
steps.note: The shape is drawn with the movement exaggerated so you can see how the part bends. Use the slider to change the scale.

steps.title: Read the von Mises stress
steps.command: Results in the browser > Von Mises Stress
actions: Double click Von Mises Stress in the browser.
Display panel: tick Maximum to show where the highest stress is.
Compare it with the yield strength of the material.
steps.note: Maximum von Mises stress: 20.9 MPa (yield strength 250 MPa). Stress right at the edge of a fixed face can read higher than real life, because a fixed face is perfectly rigid; look at the stress just away from it too.

steps.title: Read the displacement
actions: Double click Displacement.
Use Result panel > Animate to watch the part deflect under load.

steps.title: Check the safety factor
steps.command: Results in the browser > Safety Factor
actions: Double click Safety Factor. Inventor divides the yield strength by the stress at every point.
Anywhere below 1 would yield. Most designs aim for 2 or more.

steps.title: Write the report
steps.command: Stress Analysis tab > Report panel > Report
actions: Click Report. Choose the study, a format (HTML or Word) and where to save it. Click OK.
The report lists the material, the constraints, the loads, the mesh and every result, with pictures.
steps.note: Hand in the report, or copy its tables into your portfolio.

hand_check: The boss is a short tube cantilever. The load acts about 28 mm above the flange: M = 3000 x 28 = 84000 N mm. For a tube 40 outside, 26 inside, Z = pi (40^4 - 26^4) / (32 x 40) = 5162 mm^3, so the bending stress at the flange is 84000 / 5162 = 16 MPa. The slot across the top weakens the end, but there the moment is small. The FEA peak, 21 MPa, is just there, round the root of the boss where it meets the flange: the sharp corner adds about a third.
